name: Beans (bush)
pests: Watch for aphids and bean beetles; use neem oil.
care: Do not prune—bush beans are determinate and compact by nature. Harvest frequently to encourage continued pod production. Avoid overwatering; soggy soil leads to root rot.

name: Beans (pole)
pests: Protect against spider mites with insecticidal soap.
care: Provide a strong trellis or pole support early. Minimal pruning; remove only damaged or diseased leaves. Pinch the growing tip once vines reach the top of their support to encourage pod set.

name: Broccoli
pests: Keep an eye out for cabbage worms and flea beetles.
care: Remove yellowing lower leaves to improve airflow. After cutting the central head, allow side shoots to grow for extended harvest. Avoid trimming too aggressively; leaves fuel head growth.

name: Brussel Sprouts
pests: Aphids and caterpillars; use row covers.
care: As sprouts begin forming, remove lower leaves below maturing sprouts. Pinch out the growing tip (top of the plant) about 3–4 weeks before final harvest to encourage sprout uniformity.

name: Cabbage
pests: Cabbage loopers and aphids; use neem oil.
care: Outer leaves should stay intact for photosynthesis until harvest. Remove only diseased or pest-damaged leaves. Mulch heavily to regulate moisture and deter pests.

name: Cauliflower
fertilizer: High nitrogen compost or fish emulsion
pests: Cabbage worms and slugs.
care: When the head begins forming, blanch by tying outer leaves over the developing curd to protect from sun/yellowing. Remove only damaged leaves.

name: Celery
pests: Aphids and slugs.
care: Keep soil consistently moist—shallow roots dry quickly. Trim damaged outer stalks to channel energy into inner growth. For blanching (tender stalks), wrap plants with paper or mound soil around stems.

name: Chives
pests: Generally pest-free.
care: Harvest by cutting outer leaves about 1 inch above soil. Regular harvesting keeps growth vigorous. Remove flower stalks unless you want seeds, as flowering reduces leaf quality.

name: Cucumber
pests: Cucumber beetles and aphids.
care: Train vertically on trellis to improve airflow and fruit shape. Pinch off side shoots if growing in limited space (otherwise let them run). Regularly remove yellow or diseased leaves.

name: Eggplant
pests: Flea beetles and spider mites.
care: Stake or cage plants to prevent branch breakage from heavy fruits. Pinch off first flowers to encourage stronger vegetative growth. Prune suckers (lower shoots) and excess leaves for better airflow.

name: Lettuce
pests: Slugs and aphids.
care: Harvest outer leaves regularly (“cut-and-come-again” method). Avoid pruning inner growing tip or the plant will stop producing. Provide shade in hot weather to prevent bolting.

name: Parsley
pests: Generally pest-free.
care: Harvest by cutting outer stems at the base; do not just snip leaves. Regular cutting encourages bushier growth. Remove flower stalks if they appear (parsley bolts in year 2).

name: Peas
pests: Aphids and weevils.
care: Provide netting/trellis support. Minimal pruning; only remove yellow/diseased leaves. Frequent harvesting encourages more pods.

name: Peppers
pests: Aphids and spider mites.
care: Pinch out the first flower buds (the 'crown buds') to encourage branching. Prune lower leaves/branches up to the first flower cluster for airflow. Stake or cage for support as fruits weigh down branches.

name: Spinach
pests: Leaf miners and aphids.
soil: Moist, well-drained, high in organic matter
care: Harvest outer leaves regularly. Do not cut central growing point to prolong production. Provide partial shade in hot weather to prevent bolting.

name: Squash (summer)
pests: Squash vine borers and aphids.
care: Train vines outward for space efficiency. Remove older, large leaves near the base for airflow/disease prevention. Harvest fruits small and often to keep plants productive.

name: Squash (winter)
pests: Squash bugs and aphids.
care: Prune lightly to manage space but keep plenty of foliage for fruit ripening. Pinch growing tips after 3–4 fruits set (on smaller varieties) to channel energy into maturing fruit. Keep vines off damp soil with mulch to prevent rot.

name: Tomatoes
pests: Tomato hornworms and aphids.
care: Indeterminate varieties: remove suckers from leaf axils (“armpits”), prune lower leaves below first flower cluster. Stake or cage for support. Determinate varieties: minimal pruning; just remove diseased/yellow leaves. Mulch and water deeply to reduce blossom-end rot.

name: Beets
pests: Protect from leaf miners and aphids.
care: Do not prune leaves unless harvesting for food (they’re edible!). Thin seedlings early to avoid crowding. Harvest greens sparingly so bulbs still develop.

name: Avocado
pests: Monitor for root rot and lace bugs.
care: Pinch young plants to encourage branching. Prune selectively to maintain open structure and airflow. Remove suckers from the base.

name: Mint
fertilizer: Compost tea or balanced organic fertilizer
pests: Watch for spider mites and aphids.
care: Harvest frequently by pinching stems. Trim flower stalks immediately to keep leaves tender. Grows aggressively—best kept in containers.

name: Cilantro
pests: Monitor for aphids and whiteflies.
care: Harvest outer leaves regularly, cut stems close to soil. Pinch off flower stalks to delay bolting. Sow successively every 2–3 weeks for continuous harvest.

name: Basil
pests: Watch for aphids and whiteflies; use insecticidal soap.
care: Pinch growing tips above a pair of leaves to encourage bushy growth. Remove flower buds as soon as they form to prolong leaf production. Harvest stems, not just single leaves, for stronger regrowth.

name: Carrot
pests: Watch for carrot flies; use row covers.
care: Do not prune foliage; it fuels root growth. Thin seedlings early to proper spacing. Harvest greens sparingly (they’re edible but stunt root growth if overcut).

name: Bell Pepper
pests: Watch for aphids and cutworms; use neem oil.
care: Pinch first flowers to encourage branching. Prune lower leaves for airflow. Stake plants for heavy fruit loads.

name: Zucchini
pests: Watch for squash bugs; use neem oil.
care: Train vines outward for space efficiency. Remove older, large leaves near the base for airflow/disease prevention. Harvest fruits small and often to keep plants productive.

name: Radish
pests: Watch for flea beetles; use row covers.
care: No pruning needed; grows quickly. Thin seedlings to prevent crowding. Harvest promptly—leaving too long leads to woody roots.

name: Kale
soil: Moist, well-drained, high in organic matter
pests: Watch for cabbage worms; use neem oil or row covers.
care: Harvest bottom leaves first, working upward. Remove yellow/damaged leaves promptly. Pinch central growing tip only if you want to limit height.

name: Green Bean
pests: Watch for aphids and bean beetles; use neem oil.
care: Provide a strong trellis or pole support early. Minimal pruning; remove only damaged or diseased leaves. Pinch the growing tip once vines reach the top of their support to encourage pod set. Do not prune—bush beans are determinate and compact by nature. Harvest frequently to encourage continued pod production. Avoid overwatering; soggy soil leads to root rot.

name: Strawberry
pests: Watch for slugs and aphids; use diatomaceous earth.
care: Remove runners (long trailing stems) if you want more fruit yield; allow some if you want propagation. Cut off old/diseased leaves after fruiting season. Mulch around plants to keep berries off soil and deter rot.
